text:
Richmond Medicaid payments for Coronavirus Diagnostic Panel services climb to $2,818 in 2024
R. C. Weaver
In 2024, Richmond Medicaid providers billed $2,818 for Coronavirus Diagnostic Panel services, according to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Medicaid Provider Spending database. This total represented a 308.4% increase from 2023, when claims for these services reached $690.
Medicaid, administered by the states and funded by both federal and state governments, provides health coverage for low-income people, seniors, children, and individuals with disabilities. As one of the biggest components of the U.S. health care system, it serves millions nationwide.
Since Medicaid dollars are sourced from taxpayers, fluctuations in local billing indicate how health care funding is distributed within a community.
The "Coronavirus Diagnostic Panel" service group comprises Medicaid-billed services categorized by care type, based on standard HCPCS and CPT code sets. For this report, each code was aligned to one service group using consistent numeric prefixes and ranges, allowing for analysis of related services while avoiding duplicate counts and maintaining ranking accuracy over time.
Though Medicaid spending grew in multiple service categories, the Coronavirus Diagnostic Panel ranked 18th by Medicaid payments in Richmond for 2024.
Across Kentucky, the Coronavirus Diagnostic Panel placed 24th statewide in total Medicaid payments that year.
From five years before 2024, Richmond's Medicaid payments for the Coronavirus Diagnostic Panel category rose by $13,989, or 83.2%. Growth accelerated in certain years, with marked year-over-year jumps seen in 2023 and 2022.
Medicaid payments for this category were distributed citywide, but most were concentrated in a small number of ZIP codes. In 2024, ZIP code 40475 accounted for the entire $2,818 in Medicaid payments for the Coronavirus Diagnostic Panel, representing 100% of the local spending in this category for the year.
In the Coronavirus Diagnostic Panel group, most Medicaid payments were linked to a few specific billing codes.
To compare, payments for this category in Richmond rose 308.4% from 2023 to 2024, while all Medicaid claim categories in the city saw a 0.5% increase during the same period.
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services data show that combined federal and state Medicaid expenditures reached about $871.7 billion in fiscal year 2023—roughly 18% of the nation’s total health spending. This was a sharp rise from $613.5 billion in 2019 prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.
This increase indicates growth of approximately 40% over just a few years, primarily due to higher enrollment and greater utilization during and following the pandemic period.
Federal budget laws enacted under the Trump administration have included major proposals to cut federal Medicaid funding and change the program structure. One example, the “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,” signed in 2025, is expected to decrease federal Medicaid expenditures by over $1 trillion during the next decade. The law adds requirements like work mandates and increased cost-sharing, which could shrink both coverage and funding for some recipients. As a result, states may bear more costs, and overall growth in federal Medicaid assistance could decline while the program remains critical for tens of millions of Americans.
